title: Review (job model)
summary: The review daemon ticks every 120s, discovers PRs owed an independent review (or re-armed after a fix), and dispatches each as a detached, deterministic job (not a Claude wrapper session): claim a job slot, acquire a lane, run one review-loop-cli.mjs round under a hard 45-minute timeout, classify the outcome, swap the PR's review:* label, release the lane, and — only after that arc fully finishes — run advisory non-Claude extra seats. Round-cap exhaustion, a review:human park, an infra timeout, and a hard-killed job are real states with weak or missing ownership; see the notes on round-cap-exhausted, human-hold, blocked-on-infra and job-died-silently.

provides.note: .operations/review-jobs lives inside the daemon's own writable clone (cwd:<daemon-clone> above), so it is writable wherever that cwd holds

states.label: PR discovered as owed a review
states.notes: Not a wait state — every 120s tick (DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS, skills-src/conveyor/review-daemon.mjs:114) re-runs reconcile-pass.mjs's runReconcilePass (scripts/conveyor/reconcile-pass.mjs:368-386) through reconcile-core.mjs's planReconcile (scripts/conveyor/reconcile-core.mjs:781-1271), which re-derives the whole plan fresh from PR labels + live sessions/jobs each time. A PR can sit here indefinitely if lanes are starved (deferredForLanes) or Claude auth is broken (deferredForAuth) — both are 'stays owed, retried next tick', never a distinct backlog.

states.label: Dispatch paused — operator's Claude login is broken

wait.for: the cheap `claude auth status --json` probe to report loggedIn:true again

escalation.how: daemon log line, exact wording pinned

states.notes: No timeout at all: the gate stays closed until either the health-watch episode closes or the direct transcript scan of the most recently dispatched session stops seeing the auth-failure text (scripts/conveyor/claude-auth-health.mjs:82-125). Every review this tick is deferred, not lost (deferredForAuth, skills-src/conveyor/review-daemon.mjs:261-268,303).

states.label: Dispatch refused — the daemon's own clone is stale (behind origin/main in code files)

wait.for: the daemon's own gated rebuild (a separate process/flow, @daemon-rebuild) to fast-forward or rebuild the clone

escalation.how: the clone's own clone-held-stale alert log named in the thrown message

states.notes: assertMainNotStale (scripts/operations/review-job.mjs:449, called from dispatchReviewJob) throws STALE_MAIN_REFUSAL_MARKER when this checkout is behind origin/main and either DIVERGED, DIRTY, off-base, or a managed clone (WE_DAEMON_MANAGED_CLONE=1 — always true for this daemon's dedicated clone, scripts/lib/main-staleness.mjs:195). A managed clone NEVER auto-fast-forwards here on purpose (scripts/lib/main-staleness.mjs:189-195) — only its own gated rebuild may move it, which is a different flow (@daemon-rebuild) this file does not model further. Non-code-only diffs are NOT stale (scripts/lib/main-staleness.mjs:200-211, #4044).

states.label: Job slot claimed, acquiring a lane

wait.for: a free lane in the shared lane pool (lane-pool.mjs acquire --wait-ms)

retries.what: consecutive no-lane deferrals for this PR, counted off its own completion record's `lane-deferrals:N` label

states.notes: There is no review-specific concurrency cap: how many review jobs can run at once is bounded only by the SHARED lane pool's acquirable count (defaultAcquirableLaneCount, skills-src/conveyor/review-daemon.mjs:418-420), which fix and ci-heal dispatches draw from too. Nothing here escalates a starved pool to an operator; it is left to the (separate) lane-starvation health smell.

states.label: review-loop-cli.mjs running one read→judge→reduce→confirm round

wait.for: the review-loop-cli.mjs child process to exit

states.notes: SIGKILL on timeout (scripts/operations/review-job.mjs:204-206, killSignal:'SIGKILL' on the spawnSync timeout option) — a hung juror or a hung git operation inside the lane is hard-killed, not merely abandoned. No retry within this one round; a fresh round only happens if the PR is re-dispatched from review-owed on a later tick.

states.label: review:accepted — auto-cleared or human-cleared
states.notes: For an agent-addressed (review:pending) PR, reviewLoopAutoConfirm answers 'accept' unattended the moment the panel verdict is ACCEPT or PREVENTION_OUTSTANDING (scripts/lib/review-loop-policy.mjs:112-116). Two advisory branches follow, both strictly AFTER this label is already live and both incapable of ever re-opening this verdict or the label: the non-blocking extra-seats-advisory branch (every accepted/bounced/parked review), and — only when the loop's own verdict is exactly `accept` (redTeamRequired, scripts/lib/jury-core.mjs:1116-1118) — the x00g3tt post-accept RED TEAM (red-team-advisory), added by PR #2735 (commit 5dcc90a11): a non-Claude call tries to break the change and a confirmed break is recorded as a miss, never a label flip.

states.label: review:changes — bounced to the author lane
states.notes: Hands off to @fix (the conveyor's fix-dispatch path); rearm-review.mjs is what eventually swaps review:changes back to review:pending (or leaves review:human alone, scripts/conveyor/rearm-review.mjs:82-84,265-304) once a repair lands, re-entering review-owed on a later tick. review:human is never removed here (scripts/review-set-label.mjs:413-414).

states.label: review:human — parked, awaiting a human's /review

wait.for: a human to run /review, or scripts/review-set-label.mjs --to=clear-human

escalation.how: label only (review:human) + the review-pr `advise` step's advisory-panel comment; no active paging
escalation.cite: scripts/lib/review-escalation.mjs:50-66; scripts/conveyor/health-smells/index.mjs (no smell targets review:human age)

states.notes: reviewLoopAutoConfirm's refusal 1 declines UNCONDITIONALLY whenever pending.of !== CONFIRM_ACTORS.AGENT (scripts/lib/review-loop-policy.mjs:74-78,113) — there is no code path that ever auto-clears review:human. Genuinely unbounded wait: reconcile-core.mjs's own permission-block precedent (awaiting-permission, scripts/conveyor/reconcile-core.mjs:706-714) shows a session CAN sit blocked for 211+ hours with only a log note; review:human has no equivalent surfaced note at all — scripts/progress-board.mjs:509 shows it as 'awaiting your clear' (rank 0, crit) on the dashboard, which IS the one human-visible signal, but nothing pages anyone or ages it into a stronger escalation.

states.label: Negotiation round cap (5) exhausted — silently refused

retries.what: rearm/advisory-comment-counted negotiation rounds (countRearmComments + countAdvisoryComments, whichever is higher)

states.notes: GAP (uncapped-retry's mirror-image: capped, but no exit). Unlike the ci-red branch's OWN cap, which pushes an operator-facing note when exhausted ('ci-heal-exhausted', scripts/conveyor/reconcile-core.mjs:932-957), the GENERIC review/fix round-cap exhaustion at line 1257-1263 pushes NO note — only a `cap-exhausted` refusal line in that tick's report (scripts/conveyor/reconcile-pass.mjs:339-360) and the daemon's own log (skills-src/conveyor/review-daemon.mjs:491). scripts/progress-board.mjs:495 still classifies this PR as ordinary 'needs-review' (info severity, 'parked for an independent review pass') — the dashboard cannot distinguish a normally-in-flight review from one stuck at cap-exhausted forever. No label flip to review:human, no notification, no owner. This is the single clearest 'review loops cap' finding the brief asked to record.

states.label: Job reported blocked-on-infra (no lane after 5 tries, loop timeout, unparseable output, or a crash)

wait.for: the 15-minute infra cool-off before this PR is treated as retryable again

retries.what: how many times a PR may cycle back through blocked-on-infra over its lifetime

states.notes: GAP (uncapped-retry). The 15-minute cool-off bounds ONE cycle, but nothing counts how many times a PR has cycled through blocked-on-infra — a persistently-unhealthy PR (a lane pool that never recovers, a review-loop-cli.mjs bug that always times out) retries forever, every 15 minutes, with no escalation. The only mechanical backstop that could notice is the daemon-owed-no-dispatch health smell (scripts/conveyor/health-smells/daemon-owed-no-dispatch.mjs:1-8,29-36), which fires on the DAEMON'S overall dispatch productivity (30-minute streak or a 60% bad-tick ratio over 30 minutes), not on one PR's own retry count.

states.label: Job's OS process was hard-killed — no completion record written

wait.for: the next reconcile-pass read to probe this job's pid and find it dead

states.notes: A SIGKILL (host reboot, OOM kill, `kill -9`) never runs review-job.mjs's own `finally` block (scripts/operations/review-job.mjs:410-423), so no `done` completion record is written and the lane lease is never released by THIS code. The stale job-record.json is pruned automatically the next time listReviewJobAgents reads it and finds the pid dead (scripts/operations/review-job-store.mjs:115-117), which frees the PR to be redispatched — but the leaked lane lease itself is reclaimed only by a SEPARATE component, the lane pool's own ghost-lease reaper, named but not implemented in this file (scripts/operations/review-job.mjs:362, '#2748'). No owner inside this flow for that leak; it is a hand-off this file only narrates.

states.label: Added non-Claude review seats (Codex extra-juror + 2 advisory lenses) run, post-verdict
states.notes: Deliberately decoupled: this step runs strictly AFTER the arc's outcome is already reported `done` and the label already swapped (scripts/operations/review-job.mjs:296-297,307-321) — a crash, a thrown kill switch, or a timeout here is captured only as a `status` field in the logged summary (scripts/operations/review-job.mjs:311-321) and can never change the verdict, never retries, and is never surfaced to an operator. This is intentional per the file's own header, not an oversight, but it is still a no-owner/no-escalation terminus for whatever the added seats found.

states.label: x00g3tt post-accept red team — Codex/Gemini try to break the accepted PR; a confirmed break is recorded as a miss, never a label change

wait.for: review-extra-seats.mjs's `red-team` subcommand to finish (one non-Claude attack call, then a Claude re-check of anything it reports)
wait.timeout: resolveSeatTimeoutMs(env) + 20*60*1000ms wall clock on the child process itself (SIGKILL on expiry, same spawnSync mechanism as the review loop and the added seats)

states.notes: Gated on redTeamRequired(verdict) (scripts/lib/jury-core.mjs:1116-1118) — only an ACCEPT verdict ever reaches this state; a bounced or parked review never does. Deliberately decoupled exactly like extra-seats-advisory: this runs strictly AFTER the review's own outcome is already reported and labelled (scripts/operations/review-job.mjs:362-364), so a crash, a thrown kill switch (WE_REVIEW_RED_TEAM=0, or WE_REVIEW_EXTRA_SEATS=0 which disables this too), or a timeout here is captured only as a `status` field on the logged summary (scripts/operations/review-job.mjs:365-373) — never retried, never escalated, never able to change the verdict or the review:* label. `foldedVerdict` (accept/changes/needs-human, jury-core.mjs#foldRedTeamVerdict) is RECORDED as evidence only — the module's own header states it is 'recorded, not enforced' in v1 (scripts/operations/review-extra-seats.mjs:37-40,682-684). A confirmed break DOES leave a durable trace beyond the log line: a `red-team-miss` evidence row for the accepting Claude seat and for the builder's model/provider (buildMissRows, scripts/operations/review-extra-seats.mjs:879-903), a 'reworked' delegation-trial row when the PR carries a delegation marker (finishRedTeamEffects, scripts/operations/review-extra-seats.mjs:945-967), and ONE advisory PR comment deduped by a trusted-author-checked marker (scripts/operations/review-extra-seats.mjs:726-733,906-924,969-983). The model never runs twice for the same (pr, head): a prior clean seat row makes a later run a `resumeRedTeam` replay that only finishes whichever effect (row / delegation trial / comment) failed last time, spending no new call (scripts/operations/review-extra-seats.mjs:735-747,989-1014,1038-1039). It shares its daily call cap and reservation ledger with the ordinary added seats (DAILY_CAP_ENV, default 40/day, scripts/operations/review-extra-seats.mjs:76-77) — if extra-seats-advisory's own calls already spent the day's budget, the red team is simply skipped for cap reasons (scripts/operations/review-extra-seats.mjs:1050-1057), which this file records as a real, not-owned/not-escalated shared-resource coupling rather than a distinct failure. This is intentional per the module's own header, not an oversight — the same shape as extra-seats-advisory's own no-owner/no-escalation terminus, so it carries no new card.

states.label: Scheduled SHADOW runner independently observes review:pending PRs — mutates nothing
states.notes: scripts/review-runner.mjs is a SEPARATE, singleton-leased pass over the SAME review:pending population, reading a DIFFERENT durable ledger (the #2639 editor↔reviewer convergence loop's jury-ledger, via readJuryLog, scripts/review-runner.mjs:145-149) than the one review-job.mjs/review-pr.mjs write. `--enforce` is hard-refused (scripts/review-runner.mjs:222-225) — it can only ever log what it WOULD do. Checked live on this host: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` contains com.we.review-daemon.plist but NO com.we.review-runner.plist and no cron entry either — despite being built as 'the scheduled process' (file header, scripts/review-runner.mjs:3-15), nothing currently schedules it; it only runs on a manual invocation. Owner is genuinely 'none' in production today.

steps.does: gh pr list (open PRs, labels/headRefOid/statusCheckRollup/comments) + claude agents --json + live review-job records, reduced by planReconcile to a dispatch/refusal/notes plan
compute (once per tick, host-global) whether the operator's Claude login is broken, via a health-episode read plus a cheap `claude auth status --json` probe
strip a stray review:pending sitting beside review:human, and a stale advisory:* label once review:human is gone — runs independently of, and before, the discover step

detached-spawn `node review-job.mjs run --pr --repo`, unref'd, stdout/stderr appended to the job's own log file; the DAEMON's own OS process cwd stays its dedicated clone — the job never chdirs into a lane

provides.name: <daemon-clone>
provides.note: the job's OWN OS process cwd; it is a plain node process with no Claude session and no Claude permission model at all

provides.name: origin/main fetched
provides.note: produced by THIS step's own call to assertMainNotStale, which fetches before it checks — not a pre-condition of this step

steps.does: decideJobClaim against the on-disk job record for this PR's slug — refuses if a live pid already holds it

provides.name: fix-claim:<pr>
provides.note: not a real lock-file lease — a job-record.json whose live pid IS the claim; named against the closest shared vocabulary entry

provides.name: <lane>
provides.note: a logical path string only — handed forward as a --cwd=<lanePath> ARGUMENT to review-loop-cli.mjs, never as this job's own process.chdir

steps.does: `node review-loop-cli.mjs --pr --repo --cwd=<lanePath> --provider=claude --json` under a fresh per-round actor id and a hard timeout

assumes.name: <lane>
assumes.note: passed as an argv flag, not the child's OS cwd (which stays <daemon-clone> per createReviewJobIo's own `node()` helper, scripts/operations/review-job.mjs:200-206) — review-loop-cli.mjs's own internal io resolves file/git reads against the FLAG value

steps.does: spawn the correctness and security jurors as independent `claude -p` processes with Bash/Read/Grep/Glob tool access, one per mandatory lens

assumes.name: <lane>
assumes.note: assertLaneCwd THROWS (fail-closed) unless this juror's own process cwd resolves to a real lane clone, and refuses if it is the driving session's own lane

steps.does: reviewLoopAutoConfirm answers the agent-addressed confirm step (accept / changes), review-pr's record step swaps the review:* label and stamps the reviewed-sha marker via review-set-label.mjs

spawn review-extra-seats.mjs (an extra Codex correctness juror + up to 2 advisory-lens seats on Codex/Gemini), strictly after the arc's own outcome is already reported and labelled — deliberately advisory-only: a failure here is captured as a status string and never propagates (see the extra-seats-advisory state's own notes)

spawn `review-extra-seats.mjs red-team` as its own process; inside, redTeamEnabled() checks both kill switches first, then a prior clean seat row for this exact (pr, head commit) short-circuits into a `resumeRedTeam` replay (no new call spent) — otherwise selectReviewSeatProvider picks Codex or Gemini for the `red-team` lens (skipping a provider whose CLI is missing or sitting out a quota hold), reserves ONE call against the shared daily cap under the reservation-ledger lock, builds a throwaway scratch clone fetching ONLY the PINNED head commit (refuses an unpinned rev — the lane is already released by this point), and runs the attack call at the higher 'high' effort each provider offers

for every break the seat call reported, spawn a fresh tool-free Claude juror (sonnet, high effort, $1 budget, 10-minute timeout) that judges ONLY the diff to decide whether the claimed break is real; a claim it does not confirm, and a re-check that itself errors or times out, is marked `confirmedByRecheck:false` — a miss is only ever inferred from a positive confirmation, never from silence

write the red-team's own scorecard evidence row, plus one `red-team-miss` row for the accepting Claude seat and one for the builder's model per confirmed break; log a 'reworked' delegation-trial row when the PR carries a delegation marker; and post ONE deduped advisory PR comment (a trusted-author-checked marker stops a repeat post) — none of this ever swaps the review:* label, changes the merge outcome, or re-opens the round loop
